title: PROSTAGOAL: Physical and Psychosocial Effects of a Structured Recreational Football Exercise Program in Patients with Prostate Cancer Undergoing Long-Term Antiandrogen Therapy
summary:
Prostate cancer is a common cancer in men. Many patients require long-term antiandrogen therapy, also called androgen deprivation therapy. This treatment reduces the effect of male sex hormones, but it can also cause burdensome side effects. These may include tiredness and fatigue, low mood, loss of muscle and bone mass, and changes in metabolism. As a result, quality of life can be significantly affected.
The planned study will investigate whether a structured recreational football training program is feasible and safe for men with prostate cancer undergoing antiandrogen therapy. Football may offer several advantages: it is familiar to many people, can be motivating in a group setting, and combines physical activity with social interaction.
Patients with bone metastases are often unsure whether exercise is suitable or safe for them. This concern is understandable, as many patients assume that physical activity, especially team sports, may increase the risk of injury. At the same time, regular physical activity may help maintain muscle strength, physical fitness, and possibly bone health. For this reason, the training program in this study will be supervised by sports medicine professionals to support safe participation.
The study is important for several reasons. It will examine whether a team-based football exercise program can improve quality of life and psychological well-being. It will also explore whether physical fitness, cardiovascular health, and metabolic parameters may be positively affected. In addition, the study will assess whether a popular team sport such as football can be used as supportive care in cancer patients.
The aim of this pilot study is to assess whether such a training program can be organized and carried out at the Berlin study site. The study will also provide first insights into the possible effects of the program on quality of life and selected physical health parameters.
Men with histologically confirmed prostate cancer undergoing androgen deprivation therapy can be included. Before starting the program, participants will undergo a sports-medical assessment. They will then take part in a structured, supervised recreational football training program for 6 months. Assessments, including medical examinations and quality-of-life questionnaires, will be performed at the beginning of the study and after 3 and 6 months.
The main aim of the study is to assess feasibility. Feasibility will be measured by training adherence, defined as participation in at least 70% of the training sessions on average. Additional outcomes include possible effects of the training program on physical fitness and quality of life.

interventions.name: Prospective single-arm pilot study investigating the feasibility and the effects of a structured, supervised football training program on physical and psychosocial factors in men with metastatic prostate cancer undergoing antiandrogen therapy.
